checks.title: Page loads successfully
checks.rationale: Prerequisite for everything else: a 2xx response and a load event within the budget.
checks.remediation: Fix the HTTP error or slow load; make the page reach load within the timeout.

checks.title: No bot challenge blocks automated browsers
checks.rationale: Access errors, CAPTCHAs and loading failures are the largest failure class for agents on live sites (Online-Mind2Web: 51%). A challenge page is a hard stop for every agent.
checks.remediation: Exempt well-behaved agents (honest UA, Web Bot Auth signatures) from challenges on public pages, or serve a machine-readable alternative.

evidence.note: UA-parity probe with the tool's own user agent

checks.title: The DOM settles after load
checks.rationale: Agents act on a snapshot; if the DOM keeps mutating or shifting, refs go stale and clicks land on moved elements (documented for Playwright MCP and agent-browser).
references: INFERENCE thresholds: 50/300 mutations in 2 s, CLS 0.1/0.25
checks.remediation: Finish rendering before load, avoid late-inserted banners/ads, reserve space for async content, stop polling updates when idle.

evidence.observed: 0 mutations in the 2 s after settle, CLS 0
0 mutations in the 2 s after settle, CLS 0

checks.title: Network activity settles
checks.summary: Network idle reached on all pages.
checks.rationale: Agent harnesses wait for network idle; pages that never go idle (polling, SSE, WebSockets) hang or time out those waits.
references: agent-browser README: networkidle hangs on SSE/WebSockets
checks.remediation: Defer long-polling/streaming connections until after first interaction, or keep them off the initial load.

checks.title: No runtime errors during load
checks.rationale: Uncaught exceptions and failed script loads correlate with controls that do nothing when activated (INFERENCE).
checks.remediation: Fix uncaught exceptions and failed script requests reported during load.

checks.title: Interactive controls have accessible names
checks.summary: 0 of 34 interactive controls (0%) have no accessible name.
checks.rationale: Accessibility-tree agents (Playwright MCP, Chrome DevTools MCP, agent-browser) select controls by role and accessible name; an unnamed control is unselectable and grounding errors are a top failure cause in WebVoyager/Online-Mind2Web.
checks.remediation: Give every button, link and form control a visible text label or an aria-label/aria-labelledby. For icon buttons use aria-label; for inputs use <label for>.

checks.title: Clickable elements are real controls, not generic elements
checks.summary: 2 clickable elements without a control role (6% of clickables).
checks.rationale: A div/span with a click handler appears in the accessibility tree as "generic" (at best with cursor=pointer). Tree-based agents list controls by role, so such elements are invisible or ambiguous to them.
checks.remediation: Use <button> or <a href> for actions and navigation. If a custom element must stay, add role="button", tabindex="0", a name and keyboard handlers.

checks.title: ARIA attributes and roles are valid
checks.rationale: Invalid ARIA produces a misleading tree: wrong roles, missing required children, hidden-but-focusable nodes. Lighthouse's agent tree audit fails on these rules.
checks.remediation: Fix the reported ARIA usage: valid roles, required attributes/children, no aria-hidden on focusable content.

checks.title: Control names are specific, not repeated or generic
checks.summary: 6 generic names and 0 names reused for different destinations.
checks.rationale: Several links named "Read more" leading to different pages, or buttons all named "Submit", force an agent to guess; benchmarks attribute many wrong clicks to such ambiguity.
checks.remediation: Make link and button text describe the destination or action ("Read the return policy", "Add Trail Bike to cart"). Avoid "Click here"/"Read more"; use aria-label to disambiguate when visual text must stay short.

checks.title: Visible labels are part of accessible names
checks.summary: 2 controls whose accessible name does not contain their visible label.
checks.rationale: Vision-based agents read the visible label and tree-based agents read the accessible name; when they differ, agents fail to agree on which control to use.
checks.remediation: Ensure the accessible name (aria-label) contains the visible text of the control.

evidence.expected: Elements must have their visible text as part of their accessible name
evidence.note: Text inside the element is not included in the accessible name

evidence.expected: Elements must have their visible text as part of their accessible name
evidence.note: Text inside the element is not included in the accessible name

checks.title: Pages have a descriptive title and a language
checks.rationale: Agents use the title to confirm navigation succeeded and the language to interpret content; generic titles ("Home") make URL/title-based verification unreliable.
checks.remediation: Set a unique, descriptive <title> per page ("Return policy – Northwind Bikes") and <html lang="…">.

checks.title: Headings form a usable outline
checks.rationale: Agents and screen readers navigate by headings; a missing h1 or skipped levels hide the page structure.
checks.remediation: One h1 per page naming the page; nest h2/h3 without skipping levels; no empty headings.

checks.title: Images carry alternative text
checks.rationale: Tree-based agents only know an image by its alt text; images inside links/buttons without alt leave the control unnamed.
checks.remediation: Add alt text to informative images (alt="" for decorative ones); name SVG icons with aria-label or <title>.

checks.title: Accessibility snapshot fits an agent context budget
checks.rationale: Agent harnesses truncate or reject very large accessibility trees; pages above roughly 10k tokens are partially invisible to the agent.
references: Playwright MCP / agent-browser snapshot filtering docs
checks.remediation: Reduce DOM size on key pages: paginate long lists, lazy-render off-screen sections, remove duplicated hidden menus.

checks.title: Page regions are exposed as landmarks
checks.rationale: A single main landmark and a navigation landmark let an agent skip chrome and find content; agent snapshots group nodes by landmark.
checks.remediation: Wrap primary content in <main>, site navigation in <nav aria-label="…">, and header/footer in <header>/<footer>.

evidence.expected: All page content should be contained by landmarks
evidence.note: Some page content is not contained by landmarks

evidence.expected: All page content should be contained by landmarks
evidence.note: Some page content is not contained by landmarks

checks.title: Navigation links are named and resolvable
checks.summary: 10 navigation links are named and resolvable.
checks.rationale: Agents prefer navigating by following named links or by URL; nav links with href="#" or javascript: cannot be followed by URL and unnamed ones cannot be chosen.
checks.remediation: Use real URLs in href for navigation items; name every nav link; if JavaScript handles navigation, keep a working href as fallback.

checks.title: Menus do not depend on hover
checks.summary: 12 navigation links are only revealed on hover.
checks.rationale: Hover-revealed submenus are absent from the accessibility snapshot until a pointer hovers; text-first agents never see them (INFERENCE heuristic: nav links in the DOM but not in the snapshot, with no toggle button).
references: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus
Agent tooling docs: hover-only menus listed as a failure mode
checks.remediation: Expose submenus through a <button aria-expanded> toggle, or render submenu links in the page (footer sitemap) so they are reachable without hover.

evidence.expected: submenu behind a button with aria-expanded, or always rendered
submenu behind a button with aria-expanded, or always rendered

checks.title: Common destinations are discoverable from the start page
checks.summary: Found contact, help, search; missing about, privacy, terms.
checks.rationale: The most common agent goals on a site (contact, help, policies, search, pricing) should be reachable through recognisably named links from the entry page.
references: Benchmark task archetypes (WebVoyager, Mind2Web): find contact/policy/help pages
checks.remediation: Link contact, help/FAQ, privacy/terms, and search from the header or footer with their conventional names.

checks.title: Site search is exposed
checks.summary: Search exposed via search landmark/input, named search box.
checks.rationale: A labelled search box (or a schema.org SearchAction) is the fastest route for an agent to locate content on larger sites.
checks.remediation: Expose search as <form role="search"> with a labelled <input type="search">, and declare a SearchAction in WebSite JSON-LD.

checks.title: A sitemap is published
checks.summary: No sitemap.xml and no Sitemap directive in robots.txt.
checks.rationale: Crawling agents discover pages through sitemap.xml; it is the cheapest structural map of a site.
checks.remediation: Publish /sitemap.xml and reference it with a Sitemap: line in robots.txt.

checks.title: Inner pages expose breadcrumbs
checks.summary: No pages deeper than one level were scanned; breadcrumbs not expected.
checks.rationale: Breadcrumbs tell an agent where it is in the hierarchy and how to go up; schema.org BreadcrumbList does the same for fetch-based agents.
checks.remediation: Add <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb"> with links on inner pages and BreadcrumbList JSON-LD.

checks.title: Form fields have labels and names
checks.summary: 6 form fields are labelled and named.
checks.rationale: Agents fill forms by matching field labels to the data they hold; unlabelled fields force guessing and write tasks already succeed far less often than read tasks in benchmarks.
references: Web Bench: write tasks 46.6% vs read >70%
checks.remediation: Associate every input/select/textarea with a <label for>, give fields a name attribute, and use autocomplete tokens for common data.

checks.title: No overlay blocks the page at load
checks.summary: 2 overlays block the page without an accessible dismiss control.
checks.rationale: Consent banners and modals intercept clicks; agents whose click lands on the overlay loop or fail. A dismiss control with a clear name is the minimum for recovery.
references: agent-browser README: clicks fail under consent banners
BrowserArena / GUI-Robust: pop-up and cookie-consent anomalies
checks.remediation: Avoid full-page overlays at load; if a consent dialog is required, make it a role="dialog" with a clearly named Accept/Reject button and let the rest of the page work beneath it.

evidence.observed: overlay covering 100% of the viewport with no named dismiss control
evidence.note: × We use cookies This fixture shows a consent overlay whose only dismiss control is an unlabelled di

evidence.observed: overlay covering 100% of the viewport with no named dismiss control
evidence.note: × We use cookies This fixture shows a consent overlay whose only dismiss control is an unlabelled di

checks.title: Controls are native or complete ARIA widgets
checks.rationale: Custom sliders, date pickers, drag-and-drop and div-based dropdowns are the controls agents fail on most (WILBUR, WebGames); native inputs are operable through standard actions.
references: WebGames / WILBUR failure analyses: sliders, date pickers, drag-drop
checks.remediation: Prefer native <select>, <input type="date|range|number">; when custom widgets are unavoidable, implement the full ARIA pattern (roles, states such as aria-valuenow/aria-expanded, keyboard support).

checks.title: Required fields are marked programmatically
checks.rationale: An asterisk in the label is invisible to tree agents; required/aria-required tells them which fields must be filled before submitting.
checks.remediation: Add the required attribute (or aria-required="true") to mandatory fields.

checks.title: Controls are keyboard operable
checks.rationale: Agents press keys to submit forms and operate menus; positive tabindex and unfocusable controls break that sequence.
checks.remediation: Remove positive tabindex values; make custom controls focusable with tabindex="0" and handle Enter/Space.

checks.title: Controls are not confined to cross-origin iframes
checks.summary: No controls confined to cross-origin iframes.
checks.rationale: Several agents cannot act inside cross-origin iframes (documented for Comet; refs are frame-scoped in Playwright), so controls there are unreachable.
references: Research/01 §13: Comet cannot act in cross-origin iframes
checks.remediation: Keep primary actions (search, checkout, contact) in the top document; if an embedded widget is required, offer an equivalent same-origin path.

checks.title: No controls hidden in closed shadow roots
checks.rationale: Closed shadow roots are not traversable by DOM-based agents; some tree agents cannot act on their content.
references: Research/01 §14: closed shadow DOM failure mode
checks.remediation: Use open shadow roots for components that contain controls.

checks.title: The UI is not rendered only on canvas
checks.rationale: Canvas/WebGL interfaces expose no accessibility tree, so tree-based agents see nothing to act on.
checks.remediation: Provide DOM equivalents (fallback content, ARIA, or a parallel HTML UI) for canvas-rendered controls.

checks.title: Targets are large enough
checks.rationale: Vision-based agents (screenshot + coordinates) miss tiny targets; documented in computer-use guidance.
checks.remediation: Make interactive targets at least 24×24 CSS px with spacing.

checks.title: robots.txt lets user-triggered agents fetch the page
checks.summary: User-triggered agents may fetch this page.
checks.rationale: User-triggered agent fetchers (ChatGPT-User, Claude-User, search bots) honour robots.txt; disallowing them makes the site unusable to those agents regardless of its UI. Training crawler policy is a separate owner choice and is reported as info.
checks.remediation: Allow the user-triggered agent tokens (or at least * for public pages). Keep training-crawler rules separate: User-agent: GPTBot / ClaudeBot groups.

evidence.note: informational: training policy is the owner's choice

checks.title: Content is available without executing JavaScript
checks.summary: 100% of rendered text is present without JavaScript.
checks.rationale: Fetch-based agents and most AI crawlers read the HTML response without running scripts (INFERENCE from vendor documentation); a client-only app is empty to them.
checks.remediation: Server-render or pre-render the primary content; keep key text, links and forms in the initial HTML.

evidence.observed: 719 chars of text in raw HTML vs 654 rendered (110%)
evidence.expected: ≥ 50% of the rendered text present in HTML

checks.title: Structured data (JSON-LD) describes the page
checks.rationale: schema.org JSON-LD gives fetch-based agents entities (organisation, products, offers, contact points, FAQs) without parsing the layout.
checks.remediation: Add JSON-LD for Organization/WebSite on the home page and Product/Offer, FAQPage, ContactPoint or BreadcrumbList on inner pages.

evidence.expected: Organization, WebSite, WebPage, Product, Offer, FAQPage

checks.title: llms.txt is published and well-formed
checks.rationale: llms.txt is a proposed index of a site for language models. Publication is cheap and checked by Lighthouse; actual consumption by agents is UNVERIFIED (Ahrefs: 97% of files get no requests), hence the low weight.
checks.remediation: Publish /llms.txt with an H1, a one-paragraph blockquote and H2 sections of markdown links to the most useful pages.

checks.title: WebMCP tools are exposed
checks.rationale: WebMCP (W3C WebML Community Group draft, Chrome origin trial) lets a page register typed tools for agents. It is early, so absence is informational; presence is a strong signal of agent intent.
references: W3C WebML CG WebMCP explainer/spec (document.modelContext.registerTool, form[toolname])
checks.remediation: Optional: register tools via document.modelContext.registerTool({ name, description, inputSchema, execute, annotations }) or annotate forms with toolname/tooldescription.

evidence.note: WebMCP is an origin trial; absence is not penalised

checks.title: Agent manifests (agent-card, UCP, ARD) are published
checks.rationale: Emerging discovery files: A2A agent-card.json, Universal Commerce Protocol /.well-known/ucp, Agentic Resource Discovery ai-catalog.json. All are early; presence is informational.
checks.remediation: Optional: publish the manifest relevant to your domain (commerce: UCP; agent services: A2A agent card).

checks.title: No hidden instructions aimed at AI agents
checks.summary: No instruction-like hidden text (0 hidden blocks inspected).
checks.rationale: Indirect prompt injection through hidden page text is the top LLM application risk and has been demonstrated against browser agents (Brave/Comet). Text humans cannot see but agents receive is the attack surface.
references: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025: LLM01 Prompt Injection
checks.remediation: Remove hidden text that addresses AI systems; keep hidden content limited to layout helpers; do not place instructions in HTML comments or aria-hidden text.

checks.title: Consequential actions require confirmation
checks.summary: 4 of 4 consequential actions execute without a visible confirmation step.
checks.rationale: Vendors converge on a taxonomy of actions that need human confirmation (purchase, pay, transfer, send, delete, cancel, grant). A site that executes them on a single click gives an agent no safe stopping point.
references: OWASP LLM01 mitigation: human approval for high-risk operations
OpenAI Operator / Anthropic Claude for Chrome confirmation policies
checks.remediation: Put consequential actions behind a confirmation dialog (aria-haspopup="dialog" + <dialog>) or a review step; never auto-submit them.

checks.title: Forms submit safely
checks.summary: 2 forms submit to the same origin over HTTPS.
checks.rationale: An agent filling a form that posts over plain HTTP or to a third-party origin leaks data it was trusted with.
checks.remediation: Serve pages over HTTPS, post forms to the same origin over HTTPS, and never send passwords with method="get".

checks.title: WebMCP tools declare safety annotations
checks.rationale: The WebMCP draft defines readOnlyHint, consequentialHint and untrustedContentHint so agents can ask for confirmation; a mutating tool without consequentialHint, or a declarative form with toolautosubmit on a consequential action, removes that safeguard.
references: WebMCP spec: Security and Privacy considerations, ToolAnnotations
checks.remediation: Add annotations: { readOnlyHint: true } for read tools and { consequentialHint: true } for mutating tools; do not use toolautosubmit on consequential forms.

checks.title: Authentication boundaries are clearly signalled
checks.summary: No authentication forms on the scanned pages.
checks.rationale: Agents must recognise a login wall to stop and ask the user; an unlabelled password field or a credential input outside a form hides that boundary.
checks.remediation: Place credentials in a <form> with labelled fields, autocomplete="username"/"current-password", a named submit button and a heading such as "Sign in".

checks.title: No secret-looking tokens in page source
checks.rationale: An agent that reads the page source can be led to use or leak embedded credentials; patterns for common providers are detected and redacted.
references: Common secret patterns (AWS, GitHub, Stripe, OpenAI, Anthropic, Slack, private keys)
checks.remediation: Remove secrets from HTML and inline scripts; use server-side proxies or short-lived scoped tokens.

checks.title: Downloads and new windows are announced
checks.summary: 2 of 2 download/new-window links are not announced.
checks.rationale: Unexpected downloads and new windows break the single-tab model most browser agents run with; naming them lets the agent decide.
references: WCAG 2.2 G201 (advance warning for new windows)
checks.remediation: Say "(PDF)", "(download)" or "(opens in new tab)" in the link text or aria-label.
